title: Heterogeneous thermal-aware drain contract for capacity-safe Dedicated pool upgrades
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Background: As we continue rolling LTS and feature releases to Dedicated GPU pools, we've observed two correlated failure modes during drain windows: thermal-induced throttling on mixed-instance racks and autoscaler overshoot when device heterogeneity leads to imbalanced capacity accounting. Goal: design and implement a drain 'contract' layer that coordinates per-pool thermal profiles, autoscaler admission signals, and staged tenant eviction to ensure capacity-safe upgrades with minimal SLA drift. Scope: focused on Dedicated GPU pools with mixed device types (A100, H100, L40) and multi-tenant allocation. Does not include spot preemption workflows or bare-metal firmware updates (separate project). Success metrics: 1) Max p95 latency SLO drift <10% during controlled upgrades; 2) Reduction in transient pod evictions attributed to thermal throttling by >=80%; 3) Autoscaler no-longer overshoots capacity by >10% during upgrade windows. Requirements: - A signed drain contract API between rollout controller and autoscaler that supports: thermal headroom reservation, device-type-aware admission windows, and soft-preempt tokens. - Per-pool thermal telemetry feed (rolling 5m and 30m averages) surfaced to rollout controller. - Staged tenant eviction strategy honoring per-tenant QoS credits and pinned reservations. - Observable rollout gates with automatic pause/rollback on defined SLO/regression signals. - Backwards-compatible default behavior for pools without telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Drain contract API implemented and documented in runtime-2.8 spec
Autoscaler accepts and honors admission windows and thermal headroom tokens
End-to-end e2e test that simulates mixed-device pools and validates eviction pacing under thermal load
Dashboard showing thermal headroom, admission tokens, and rollout gate state for each pool
Runbook updated with drill for manual override and rollback steps
risk_register: If telemetry lag > 30s, thermal headroom tokens may be stale -> fallback to conservative drain rate
Incorrect device-type inventory could cause admission windows to be overly permissive for some tenants
Rollout controller bug could block all admission tokens leading to pool-wide capacity starvation
next_steps: Finalize API schema with autoscaler and rollout-controller owners (meet Wed 2026-03-03)
Instrument per-pool thermal feed prototype (infra spike, 2d)
Write e2e simulation harness to inject thermal events and verify pacing logic
Create canary plan for single low-risk pool with synthetic tenant workloads
